access_policy.captured_here: documented public unauthenticated market-data endpoints only

coverage_assessment.assets_required: BTC and ETH (or another supported alt)

families_absent.MECHANICAL_BASIS: no captured endpoint publishes a provider-native basis field; every basis is derived, and deriving one is not authorized

label: SECOND-AGENT TECHNICAL AUDIT - NOT ORGANIZATIONALLY INDEPENDENT

raw_storage.repo_policy: raw bytes are NOT committed; only this manifest and its checksums are

readiness_impact.reason: a capture proves what the provider returned at one instant; it does not prove what the field means, and no fixture was promoted
what_the_captures_do_support: OKX publishes oi, oiCcy and oiUsd together and they are arithmetically separable, which confirms the r1 Tier-A claim that one canonical oi_native would merge three distinct quantities
OKX fundingTime is a FUTURE settlement instant relative to ts, and nextFundingRate is an empty string that must not be coerced to zero
Kraken publishes two funding fields differing by ~the index price, so one is not a per-interval fraction; the payload does not say which
Kraken returns orderbook bids WORST-FIRST (measured: 1147 levels, first element 1, best bid 59900), so a best-first consumer must reverse
Gate carries funding_interval and quanto_multiplier as contract metadata, so the interval is available for that venue only
Deribit reports open interest as a USD notional, a different native unit from a contract count

limitations: contract face value / multiplier is NOT in the payload, so converting oi to oiCcy requires contract terms
the three-field relationship is measured arithmetically, not documented in this capture
one sample: proves field shape, proves nothing about revisions or backfill

native_units.oi: CONTRACT_COUNT (MEASURED: oi != oiCcy and oi/oiCcy is not asset-constant)
native_units.oiUsd: USD_NOTIONAL (MEASURED: oiUsd/oiCcy equals the contemporaneous price)

records.semantic_claim: Three separate native quantities (contract count, base-coin quantity, USD notional) are published for one observation, so a single canonical oi_native would merge three different measurements.

timestamp_semantics.scope: point-in-time snapshot; no interval window is published

limitations: contract face value is not in the payload
records.semantic_claim: On an inverse swap the same three fields appear but oi/oiCcy is a different constant than on the linear swap, so the ratio is contract-type dependent and a contract count is not a coin quantity.
The three-quantity shape is not BTC-specific.

limitations: the funding interval in seconds is NOT in the payload; it must come from contract terms
nextFundingRate was empty in this capture and must not be coerced to 0
records.semantic_claim: fundingTime is a FUTURE settlement instant relative to ts, so a reader that treats it as the time the rate became known back-dates or forward-dates the observation; and nextFundingRate is an empty string, which is not zero.

timestamp_semantics.fundingTime: the NEXT settlement instant of the CURRENT period (ms epoch), i.e. AFTER ts
timestamp_semantics.scope: current period only; this is not a funding history row

records.semantic_claim: The future-settlement convention and the empty predicted slot are not BTC-specific.

timestamp_semantics.fundingTime: next settlement of the current period (ms epoch), after ts

limitations: level quantity unit is declared, not separable inside the payload

native_units.levels[1]: CONTRACT_COUNT (DECLARED for swaps; not separable inside this payload)

records.semantic_claim: A REST book is a bounded snapshot with its own sequence id and a level schema longer than price/size, so it cannot certify a full-depth book and level[1] is not base coin.

timestamp_semantics.scope: bounded top-of-book snapshot, NOT full depth
timestamp_semantics.seqId: provider sequence id of this snapshot

limitations: per-level notional-to-contract relationship depends on contract specification
records.semantic_claim: On an inverse perpetual the level amount is a USD notional, and the snapshot carries a change_id that a later chain would have to continue from.
The inverse-notional level shape is not BTC-specific.

limitations: the notional is provider-computed; it is not a base-coin exposure

native_units.open_interest: USD_NOTIONAL (DECLARED for inverse; MEASURED: open_interest/mark_price is a plausible coin quantity)

records.semantic_claim: Deribit publishes open interest already denominated in USD, a different native unit from a contract count, so the two cannot share one canonical slot.

limitations: this document is contract metadata, so a capture is not a funding observation with an event time
records.semantic_claim: Gate publishes the funding interval and the contract multiplier as contract metadata in the same document as the rate, so the interval is available for a linear contract here while several other venues do not publish it at all.

timestamp_semantics.funding_next_apply: epoch SECONDS of the next settlement
timestamp_semantics.scope: contract specification, not a per-observation history row

limitations: total_size must be scaled by quanto_multiplier from the contract document to reach a coin quantity
the ticker carries no event time

native_units.total_size: CONTRACT_COUNT (MEASURED: total_size * quanto_multiplier is a plausible coin quantity)

records.semantic_claim: Gate's open interest lives on the ticker document under total_size as a contract count, while the contract document (a different endpoint) carries the multiplier needed to interpret it.

timestamp_semantics.scope: ticker state; the ticker document carries no per-observation event time

records.docs: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/futures-api/ (GET /derivatives/api/v3/tickers; ?symbol= filter returned an empty list, so the multiplexed document is captured whole)
limitations: the two funding fields' conventions are NOT established by this capture
the response multiplexes every listed instrument, so isolation is a local step
records.semantic_claim: Kraken publishes TWO funding fields whose magnitudes differ by four orders, so at least one of them is not a per-interval fraction; the payload does not say which convention either uses. Both mark and index price are also present, so a reader must not attribute either price by position.

timestamp_semantics.lastTime: provider last update time (ISO-8601, nanosecond precision)

limitations: quantity unit is declared, not separable inside the payload
bids arrive ascending, so a best-first consumer must reverse them
records.semantic_claim: A Kraken orderbook snapshot is available on the live PF_ symbol but not the retired PI_ symbol, and its bids are published WORST-FIRST (ascending price), so bids[0] is the deepest bid rather than the best one.

timestamp_semantics.scope: snapshot; no per-level timestamp is carried
